blocks.x: Zero-trust across a converged network estate, attack paths into core systems cut by 92% and MTTR for network incidents down 44%

A tier-1 European telecom operator: Operators feel decision gaps in churn and support volume, both visible in monthly cohorts. The Achala program started with the subscriber journey —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline assessment drew the flatness honestly: 640 attack paths from corporate IT to network-operations systems, 78% of admin access standing rather than just-in-time, and incident forensics taking days because logs lived in per-vendor silos.
The constraint was operations: OSS platforms could not blink. Previous segmentation attempts had died in change freezes.

We sequenced zero-trust around operations: identity-first waves with JIT admin access, segmentation designed per OSS platform with vendor sign-off and fallback drills, network-IT boundary enforced with session recording on every admin path, and a unified detection spine so forensics reads one timeline. Change freezes became wave gates rather than excuses.
